chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Herman Chittison's career and travels
summary: Chittison left the U.S. in the late 1920s and travelled in Europe and India, working for Jacoby; he settled in Ohio.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Okay. Not too much is - maybe I shouldn't say that. I don't know too much about Herman Chittison, maybe one or two of his records. That's about all.
Yeah well, Herman didn't make allot of recordings.
I know he played in Paris, I think, for a long time.
Chittison had already, he had also worked for Herbert Jacoby at the Ruban Bleu.
I see.
But Herman Chittison was one of the musicians that left the United States very early in the era. I would say he probably left the United States

in the late '20s. And he traveled all over Europe. He played in India, Egypt, and all around. You know, once the performance got over there you just traveled and traveled. He had been everywhere. But when he came back he went into the Rue Ban Bleu. He was secure there. And he had the style, sort of similar to Art Tatum, but he wasn't that commercially inclined. He didn't care whether he recorded or not. There are allot of musicians, good musicians, a lot of good music that has never been recorded because that's another thing altogether, you know, trying to make records and trying to be recognized. And so, there was a record that came out, oh after nobody was making records that Musicraft, there was a label Musicraft, it started in - I don't know exactly what year, but they recorded some what they considered I suppose quality stuff. And they had absolutely no success at it. But later on in the '50s I had made recordings and allot of people hadn't - I ran across an album that has some of the material in there that Musicraft had recorded. Somebody bought out the inventory and recorded it.
